title: Design System: David Candela — Cybersecurity Journey

display.purpose: Page and section H1 headers. Playfair Display only. Used once per major section, never stacked.

headline.purpose: H2 section anchors within content. Playfair Display only.

body.purpose: Default reading rhythm. DM Sans. Max line length 65-75ch.

label.purpose: Category markers, skill group headings, meta text. The only uppercase treatment in the system.

code.purpose: Inline and block code. Fira Code.

shadows.name: ambient-low
shadows.purpose: Cards and containers on hover. Lowest visible elevation signal.

shadows.name: ambient-mid
shadows.purpose: Modal or sheet surfaces. Focussed interactive cards.

shadows.name: ambient-high
shadows.purpose: Topmost elevated overlay. Reserved for surfaces that must visually float above content.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions. Ease-out-quart feel.

narrative.overview:
This system belongs to someone who spent 13 years at Apple and brought that standard with them. It does not announce itself. The cream backgrounds, the disciplined type scale, the single accent color held in reserve: every decision reflects the same principle as the content itself. The work is the credential. The design is the proof of care.

The palette is warm and physical, not digital-clinical. Playfair Display handles section headers with authoritative weight; DM Sans handles the body and UI with clean utility. The Harvest Mark orange is the only saturated voice. On any given screen it covers 8-12% of the surface. Its rarity is load-bearing.

This system explicitly rejects the generic dark hacker aesthetic: Matrix green on black, terminal-green glows, neon on dark.
keyCharacteristics: Single orange accent, used at controlled density
Flat by default; shadow only on interactive state change
Uppercase-tracked labels as the only typographic ornamentation
No gradients, no glassmorphism, no side-stripe borders

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Harvest Mark is the only saturated color in the system. It appears on ≤12% of any screen. Its rarity is what makes it mean something.

rules.name: The Warmth Rule
rules.body: Never use pure white (#fff) or pure black (#000) as surfaces or text. The cream neutrals are tinted toward the brand hue. A pure-white background instantly breaks the register.

rules.name: The Uppercase Limit Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is only legal at label scale (0.78rem) with tracked letter-spacing (0.09em). Any uppercase element at body size or larger breaks the system's register.

rules.name: The Serif Boundary Rule
rules.body: Playfair Display is for H1 and H2 only. H3 and below use DM Sans. Allowing serif to bleed down the hierarchy dilutes the weight contrast the system relies on.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A card at rest has no shadow. A border defines its edge. When the user hovers, Ambient Low appears. Static shadows are visual noise.

dos: Do use Harvest Mark (#C96B3A) as the single accent. Links, active states, the tab indicator, admonition icons.
Do keep Harvest Mark at ≤12% surface coverage per screen.
Do default every surface to Warm Cream (#FAF7F2), not white.
Do use Warm Cream Mid (#F0EBE1) for secondary surfaces: code blocks, pill backgrounds, table headers.
Do use Playfair Display for H1 and H2 only.
Do uppercase labels only at 0.78rem with 0.09em tracking.
Do keep surfaces flat at rest. Apply Ambient Low shadow only on hover or interactive state.
Do cap body line length at 65-75ch.
donts: Don't use Matrix green, terminal-green, neon on dark, or any dark hacker aesthetic. This is the primary anti-reference.
Don't introduce a second saturated accent alongside Harvest Mark.
Don't use pure white (#fff) or pure black (#000) as surface or text values.
Don't add shadows to surfaces at rest.
Don't use glassmorphism: frosted blur cards, translucent panels, backdrop-filter for decoration.
Don't place Playfair Display below H2.
Don't use uppercase at body size or larger.
Don't use a side-stripe border (border-left or border-right > 1px) as a colored accent on cards or callouts.
Don't present this as a resume template or revert to a corporate SaaS look.
